role: The SwiftUI App declaration: builds the root singletons (collector, sync, settings, StoreKit, language, voice chat, Watch bridge) as @State, assembles the root view (MainTabView + environment + launch modals + scene-phase handlers + interrupted-session alerts + launch tasks), wires Watch->phone control closures, and holds the @main entry EmuquMain.
types: LaunchModal: enum — which full-screen launch cover is up (disclaimer/onboarding/paywall/trialReminder/scoreArchitectureChange)
InterruptedSessionInfo: struct — a recording found persisted at launch; isResumable gates the resume alert
EmuquApp: struct (App) — app root; extended by AppLaunchTasks.swift and AppLaunchRecovery.swift
EmuquMain: enum (@main) — process entry, runs UI-test wipe + crash handlers before EmuquApp.main()
state: mem:coldStartLog (file-private OSLog subsystem com.chrissharp.flowrecovery category ColdStart)
toplevel: Stored-property initializers of EmuquApp call the seven makeX() factories (EmuquApp.swift:86-99), so every root singleton is built when EmuquApp.main() instantiates the App struct, after EmuquMain.main() has run the UI-test wipe and diagnostics install. emailBridge reads AssistantEmailBridge.shared directly (106). LaunchModal conforms to Identifiable for fullScreenCover(item:). Only the @State factories, emailBridge and installDiagnostics read `.shared` singletons directly (the file is whitelisted as composition root by scripts/check_no_shared_outside_root.sh); the scene-phase, launch and Watch handlers reach ambient location, power policy, morning scheduler, keyboard dismissal, recorder box and settings sync through AppDependencies.current, as the AppLaunchTasks/AppLaunchRecovery extensions do, so a test override reaches both. LaunchModal has no associated values, so it is Equatable and drives .onChange(of: activeModal).

flags.text: Two access predicates exist for the same gate: storeKitManager.hasActiveAccess (isPurchased || hasBypassGrant, StoreKitManager.swift:627) here and in presentPaywallIfNowRequired, and EmuquApp.hasAccess (AppLaunchTasks.swift:700) in paywallModal/watch refusals/startWorkoutFromWatch. They differ under -UITests-ForcePaywall: hasAccess returns false unconditionally while hasActiveAccess still honours the persisted Skip (Debug) grant (StoreKitManager.swift:540-543), so the launch gate and onboarding-completion gate can disagree in Debug UI runs.

On background, if the collector has a completed session awaiting acceptance, begins a BackgroundTaskAssertion and starts an unstructured Task that runs collector.acceptSession() (archive + baseline) and ends the assertion when it returns or throws (deferred); errors are logged only. If the background budget runs out first the assertion's expiration handler ends it, so iOS suspends the app instead of killing it.
